The war and siege states (war data, siege warfare data, capture point, turret, builder, land claim, territory interactor) read every retail body of the capture index and write it back to the same bytes.
Every war sign-up and roster call and answer of the captures (sign-up, leave, list, count, remote board, add, remove, permission, swap, move, kick) reads and writes back.
A game master declares a war between a territory's owner and another company (`!war`), gives its result or takes it back; the wars live in the world database.
Every client gets the war data in the world entity: companies, factions, territory, and the phase by the clock (scheduled, running for 30 minutes, result shown for 3 minutes).
A war whose time runs out goes to the defender; an attacker that wins takes the territory's claim.

War board: a sign-up for the side of the player's faction while the war waits gets the retail done answer, a kicked player gets the retail banned answer; leave, list, count and the remote board use get their retail answers.
Roster: 10 groups of 5 in the player's territory interactor state; the war leader and officers add, remove, swap, move, kick and set permissions, each answered as retail.

PvP faction missions give their faction influence in the mission's territory (50, 100 or 200 points from the success event); the influence lives in the world database, loses one percent about every 90 s outside a conflict and goes back to zero when a conflict ends.
Every client sees each claim's influence percent per faction, its race start, its conflict faction and start and its lottery end in the claims state.
A conflict starts 15 minutes before the owner's siege hour, at least 13 h 45 min after the race start, for the attacking faction with the most influence.

A company declares a war in a conflict (`Declare_War` right, its faction, the cost from its treasury or the player's wallet, the siege window); a refusal answers with the cost and window the server holds.
The first declaration starts a 10-minute lottery; one declaring company gets the war at the siege hour of the next day, the others get their coin back.

The claims show the war declaration threshold faction: the attacking faction whose company first earned 300 influence points in the race (the retail flips came with a rise of that faction at 3 % to 58 %, never the owner's faction); it clears when the race starts again.
A war declaration that is tried again after its answer was lost is stored once and paid once.

Each company that loses the lottery hears it: the client shows "War Declaration Unsuccessful" with the coin refund text (the client's error message with status `WarDecNotSelected`). A declaration in the lottery gets its pending notice with the layout of the client's reader.

Forts: a PvP-flagged player in a free or enemy fort's capture sphere takes it for its faction (600 s for one player, faster with a bigger lead); the claims show the fort contested, then its new owner; a fort taken outside the race window locks for one hour with its lock timer; during a conflict or a war of the territory the fort is inactive. The fort's capture point entity shows its kind, capturing faction and progress.

Influence towers: the three towers of each territory are active only in the 45 minutes before its conflict slot; a flagged player in a tower takes it (120 s, down to 75 s with a lead of 5); after the window the towers show no owner.

Each of the 39 towers sits at the entry of the claims' list that the client gives it: the client sorts the tower actor ids by their bytes and gives the first tower entry 18. The order puts every tower in its territory's group of three, and the retail captures where a player stood at a tower show the same entries.

A held tower gives its faction influence every 5 seconds in the race window, and influence gains rise by 10 % per held tower, 20 % for the held fort and 10 % for an underdog faction (two territories less than the faction with the most).
The tower texts of the client show the server's values: the remote config serves the tower influence amount and its percent bonus from the server's own influence rules.
The faction that holds a territory's fort gets 5 % more character experience while its players are in that territory (the fort's territory bonus).
No retail capture shows the fort's 5 % experience bonus yet: the one candidate (kills that gave 33 experience for 32) was a player with no faction, so it is not the fort bonus.
A running or resolved war's entry in the war data carries the world's value in its game mode field, as retail; a war that waits carries 0.

The war instance: the director opens an instance of the open world map cut to the fort's 512 m frame, with its own phase, 15 minutes before the war's start, for the forts the captures show; the roster's players get the loading screen and the instance's level with the frame, and arrive at their side's place.
The pre-raid status (715) of the war roster, as retail: a player gets selected, unselected, promoted or demoted as its roster seat changes, and war ended before the war's end in the instance.

The fort gates and walls take damage and break.

The war camps (spawn tents) of each side and the respawn wave timer as retail runs them.
